title: nf-austin/valis pipeline parameters
description: Automated whole slide image registration with VALIS (rigid + non-rigid), producing aligned ome.tiff slides

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Where the slides come from and where results go.

input.description: Samplesheet CSV listing the images to register.
input.help_text: Columns: `set` (optional) and `image`. Rows sharing a `set` are registered together **in row order**, and the first row of each set is the reference every other image is warped onto. Sets run in parallel. Omit `set` to treat the whole sheet as one set. Use this rather than `--images` when launching from Seqera Platform.

images.description: Ad-hoc alternative to a samplesheet: comma-separated, ordered list of 2+ image paths.
images.help_text: The first entry is the reference. Convenient on the command line; prefer `--input` on Seqera Platform, where a samplesheet gets a file browser. Mutually exclusive with `--input`.

name.description: Name for the registration set. Defaults to the reference image's basename.
name.help_text: Only used with `--images`, or as the fallback name for a samplesheet with no `set` column. Becomes the output subdirectory name.

outdir.description: Output directory. Use an absolute path when running on cloud storage.

crop.description: Coordinate frame of the warped outputs.
crop.help_text: `reference` gives every output the reference image's dimensions, so they stack pixel-for-pixel onto it. `overlap` crops to the region all images share. `all` keeps the union extent, padding as needed.

check_for_reflections.description: Detect and correct slides that are mirrored or flipped relative to the reference.
check_for_reflections.help_text: Off in VALIS itself. Enabling it evaluates x-flip, y-flip and x+y-flip for each adjacent pair, roughly quadrupling the rigid-stage feature work; non-rigid registration and full-resolution warping are unaffected. Arbitrary rotation is handled regardless. Turn off only if you know every slide already shares an orientation.

micro_reg.description: Run a second, higher-resolution non-rigid registration pass.
micro_reg.help_text: More accurate, noticeably slower on large slides. Disable for a quicker first look.

merge.description: Also write one merged multi-channel OME-TIFF per set.
merge.help_text: Convenient for viewers such as QuPath. Large, and most meaningful when the slides carry distinct channels.

imgs_ordered.description: Treat the input order as the z-stack order instead of letting VALIS sort by similarity.
imgs_ordered.help_text: Useful for serial sections cut in a known order.

create_masks.description: Let VALIS compute tissue and overlap masks.
create_masks.help_text: Set false if a run fails inside mask creation with a multi-Otsu thresholding error, which happens on low-contrast or near-uniform slides.

use_gpu.description: Use the CUDA container, request a GPU, and switch to a GPU-capable non-rigid registrar.
use_gpu.help_text: Requires an executor that can allocate an NVIDIA GPU. VALIS only uses CUDA for feature detection and matching, which run on heavily downsampled images, so this also switches `non_rigid_registrar` to `RAFTWarper` — otherwise the GPU would accelerate thumbnail-sized work only.

max_processed_image_dim_px.help_text: Raise to 1024 if registration fails or finds too few feature matches. Costs time and memory.

max_non_rigid_registration_dim_px.help_text: Higher is more accurate and more memory-hungry. VALIS switches to an experimental tiled registrar once it estimates more than 10 GB of in-memory images.

micro_max_dim_px.description: Working size for micro-registration. Must exceed the non-rigid size above.
micro_max_dim_px.help_text: If it does not exceed `max_non_rigid_registration_dim_px`, VALIS silently skips micro-registration; the pipeline fails up front instead.

non_rigid_registrar.description: Non-rigid registrar class from valis.non_rigid_registrars (CPU runs).

non_rigid_registrar_gpu.description: Non-rigid registrar used when --use_gpu is set. The only GPU-capable option.

valis_compression.description: OME-TIFF compression codec override. VALIS defaults to DEFLATE.

container_options.title: Container options
container_options.description: Which image the registration process runs in.

valis_container.description: Pin a specific image, overriding the automatic CPU/GPU selection.

execution_options.title: Execution environment
execution_options.description: Cluster scheduler, image caches and bind mounts. Relevant when running on HPC.
execution_options.help_text: Use the `slurm` profile together with an engine profile: `-profile slurm,singularity`. On Seqera Platform a SLURM compute environment already sets the executor, so you normally only need the cache and bind settings here.

slurm_queue.help_text: Only used with `-profile slurm`. Left unset, no --partition flag is emitted and the cluster default applies.

cluster_options.description: Raw sbatch options appended to every job, e.g. '--qos=long'.

gpu_cluster_options.description: sbatch options used to request a GPU when --use_gpu is set.
gpu_cluster_options.help_text: SLURM ignores Nextflow's `accelerator` directive, so on that executor the GPU must be requested through sbatch options. Adjust to match your site, e.g. '--gres=gpu:a100:1'.

singularity_cache_dir.description: Shared directory for pulled Singularity images.
singularity_cache_dir.help_text: Put this on shared storage the compute nodes can read. $HOME is quota-limited and is not always mounted on compute nodes. Defaults to NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR, then Nextflow's own $NXF_HOME location.

conda_cache_dir.description: Shared directory for created conda environments.

singularity_bind.description: Extra paths to bind into the container, comma-separated, e.g. '/mnt/gpfs,/scratch'.
singularity_bind.help_text: autoMounts only binds paths Nextflow itself resolved. HPC filesystems are routinely symlinked (/data -> /mnt/gpfs/...), which shows up as 'file not found' inside the container even though the host path exists. Bind the real parent here.

max_job_request_options.title: Maximum job request options
max_job_request_options.help_text: Registration requests 16 CPUs by default. On a small machine lower `--max_cpus`, or the task cannot be submitted at all.

max_cpus.description: Maximum CPUs for any single job.

max_memory.description: Maximum memory for any single job.

max_time.description: Maximum time for any single job.

help.description: Print the help message and exit.
